subject: QMon onboarding: prompt sets, eval harness integration & canary/rollback cadence
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@clearpathhealth.com>, David Cho <david.cho@clearpathhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: QMon onboarding: prompt sets, eval harness integration & canary/rollback cadence

Hi Sophie / David,

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday — excited to get ClearPath onboarded. I wanted to put a concrete starting plan on the table for our Quality Monitoring (QMon) workstream so we can align before the engineering handoff. High-level proposal below: 

1) Prompt sets
- We will take the initial prompt collection you shared and produce a canonical promptset(v1) with 250 examples across the 3 target intents (diagnosis, triage, patient-communication). CSV attached (qmon-promptset-v1.csv).
- Ownership: ClearPath provides labels and golden responses; Redwood will canonicalize and sample for canary/regression sets.

2) Eval harness integration
- We will stage an eval harness in your staging environment that runs nightly against the promptset and emits: accuracy (task-specific), hallucination flags, token-level latency distribution, and embedding-drift metrics.
- Deliverable: eval-harness-integration-checklist.md (attached) with required endpoints, auth method, and example payloads.

3) Regression alerts & metrics
- Primary signals: promptset pass-rate (macro-avg), top-1 label agreement, and hallucination rate.
- Initial thresholds: alert if pass-rate drops >2 percentage points vs baseline OR hallucination rate increases by 1.5x.

4) Canary & rollback policy
- Proposed canary window: 48 hours with at least 2,000 tokens processed or 1,000 user requests (whichever hits first).
- Rollback triggers (automated + manual): automated rollback if critical SLA (error rate OR latency P95) breaches by defined margin for >30m; manual rollback if regression on promptset >2% after human review.
- We will publish a short runbook for the canary window and rollback steps (draft attached: canary-rollback-policy-draft.pdf).

Next steps / asks from ClearPath:
- Confirm owners for labeling + who will grant staging endpoints and service account for the harness.
- Share any regulatory constraints that would require audit logs to be retained beyond standard retention.

Would you be available for a 30-min alignment call on Wednesday (May 27) 10:00–10:30 PT? If that works we’ll invite the engineering contacts and bring the draft runbook.

Thanks,

Karthik Iyer
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
+1 415-555-0182

Subject: Re: QMon onboarding: prompt sets, eval harness integration & canary/rollback cadence

Thanks Karthik — this looks good and clear. A few quick clarifying Qs before the Wed call: 

- For the canary window, does Redwood require traffic to be mirrored from prod, or can we run the canary solely against synthetic/staged traffic? We would prefer staged if possible for patient-data minimization.

- For automated rollback: you mention "critical SLA (error rate OR latency P95) breaches by defined margin for >30m" — can you confirm what "defined margin" means in practice? Is that a relative change (e.g., P95 > 1.3x baseline) or absolute?

- On retention: we have a limit on storing patient transcripts in external cloud for more than 7 days unless encrypted and access controlled. Do you have a recommended config?

FYI I attached a short compliance note that lists our internal requirements.

— Sophie
Sophie Lang
Head of Product Ops | ClearPath Health

Subject: Re: QMon onboarding: prompt sets, eval harness integration & canary/rollback cadence

Hi Sophie — quick answers and a recommended tightening of the runbook before engineering kickoff.

1) Canary traffic
- We can support both approaches. Recommended: start with staged/synthetic traffic for the first two canaries to validate metric collection and avoid PHI. Once you sign the staging-to-prod mirroring addendum (we'll push an MCP), we can move to mirrored prod traffic for subsequent canaries. Owner: ClearPath engineering to enable mirroring; Redwood will provide the hook.

2) "Defined margin" for automated rollback
- We'll use relative thresholds for adaptive sensitivity. Defaults we propose: 
  - Latency P95: >1.3x baseline for >= 30 minutes triggers an alert; >=1.5x baseline for >= 30 minutes will auto-fail the canary.
  - Promptset pass-rate: drop >= 2.0 percentage points triggers alert; drop >= 3.5 percentage points (after smoothing) will auto-fail and kick rollback.
  - Hallucination rate: 1.5x increase triggers manual review; 2.0x increase triggers auto-fail.

3) Retention & compliance
- For PHI-sensitive data: recommend token-level redaction before it leaves ClearPath environment. If you must store examples in Redwood, we can enable customer-managed KMS + audit logging and set a 7-day retention policy by default; extension possible via enterprise contract.

4) Eval harness specifics (tasks & outputs)
- We'll run nightly batch evals and a lightweight continuous stream for latency / embedding-drift. Outputs we want to capture into QMon: per-prompt score, failure reason tags (hallucination, unrelated answer, safety-red flag), and verdicts (pass/fail).

5) Responsibilities & timeline
- Week 0 (this week): Align ownership and push staging credentials.
- Week 1: Redwood builds harness connector and ingests canonical promptset v1; ClearPath validates labels.
- Week 2: First staged canary; monitoring dashboards live.

I attached a short checklist to help engineering (eval-harness-integration-checklist.md). I can add these thresholds into the runbook doc if you want.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success | Redwood Inference

Thanks all — quick alignment summary from today's call and agreed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

- Canary policy: start with 48-hour staged canary. Mirror to prod only after ClearPath signs the mirroring addendum.
- Rollback rules agreed: latency P95 auto-fail threshold = 1.5x baseline; promptset pass-rate auto-fail = 3.5 percentage points; hallucination auto-fail = 2.0x. Manual review for softer alerts.
- Alerts & notifications: Redwood will push alerts to the ClearPath PagerDuty integration; critical alerts will also create a HubSpot task (link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/98765).
- Ownership: ClearPath to provide staging service account + label validation by EOD Fri (May 29). Redwood (Marissa / Jonas) to deliver harness connector and run first staged canary in Week 2.

Action items:
- ClearPath: share staging creds and confirm retention requirements (Sophie).
- Redwood: update runbook with numeric thresholds and publish v0.1 to the shared Drive (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3Cqmon).
- Schedule: first staged canary target: week of June 7.

If that matches what you heard, I’ll mark the handoff as "ready for engineering" and kick off the Jira card.

Best,
